title.narrative: Health Services support to Secondary Care in Al-Fasher, North Darfur.

description.narrative: ltpgtRelief International (RI) and UK-MED are collaborating to address the pressing health and nutrition needs of individuals in North Darfur, particularly in El Fasher locality, focusing on stabilizing and restoring secondary healthcare services. The project will target 88,771 individuals (59,593 females and 29,178 males). ltbrgtThe project focuses on stabilizing and restoring secondary healthcare services, particularly in El Fasher Maternity Hospital. This includes operationalizing the Outpatient Department (OPD) and the Obstetrics and Gynecology departments. Services will integrate emergency trauma response, outbreak management, WASH in health facilities, mental health and psychosocial support (MHPSS), and sexual and gender-based violence (SGBV) care. RI will enhance healthcare by providing staff incentives, ensuring the availability of medical supplies (in coordination with WHO and UNICEF), procuring buffer stock, drugs, and equipment, as well as offering fuel for generators to maintain critical services such as theatre operations. Staff will receive capacity-building support, and telemedicine services will be offered in coordination with UK-MED. ltbrgtIn WASH, the project will rehabilitate critical infrastructure at El Fasher Maternity Hospital to ensure a safe, clean environment for patients and staff. Safe water will be provided for drinking, handwashing, and other hospital needs. Inclusive sanitation services will be established, including gender-segregated latrines and showers for patients, caregivers, and staff. Infection Prevention and Control (IPC) protocols will be enhanced, with provisions for medical waste management, cleaning, and sanitation supplies. ltbrgtThe nutrition component focuses on treating children under 5 suffering from severe acute malnutrition (SAM) without medical complications through the outpatient therapeutic program (OTP). The project will also address moderate acute malnutrition (MAM) in children aged 6-59 months and in pregnant and breastfeeding women and girls (PBW/G) through a targeted supplementary feeding program. Health workers will receive training on the management of SAM and MAM cases, along with Infant and Young Child Feeding (IYCF) practices. WASH kits will be provided to malnourished individuals to ensure access to essential hygiene items. Monitoring visits by the State Ministry of Health (SMOH) and RI staff will track treatment progress and offer on-the-job training to improve the quality of care. ltbrgtProtection activities are integrated and will focus on vulnerable populations, particularly women and girls. RI will establish a safe space within the hospital for women and girls, enhancing access to SGBV services and MHPSS. Specialized GBV case management will be offered, including clinical management of rape and referral support for those at risk or survivors of GBV. Services will also extend to vulnerable men and boys. ltbrgtThe project will integrate conflict sensitivity, adhering to the "do no harm" principle. This involves conducting conflict analyses, engaging communities, ensuring transparent beneficiary selection, and performing regular risk assessments. By collaborating with communities and local authorities, RI aims to promote peace and stability while delivering timely aid. ltbrgtUK-MED’s contribution involves reducing morbidity and mortality at El Fasher Hospital by providing remote support for secondary care through Multidisciplinary Teams (MDTs). MDTs will offer technical support in clinical areas and provide remote training to increase the hospital staff's capacity to identify and address gaps in care. ltbrgtMonitoring, evaluation, feedback mechanisms, and staff training will ensure that health, nutrition, and protection services are delivered effectively, without exacerbating local tensions, while adapting to the volatile environment. ltbrgtlt/pgt
